title: LLM4OM documentation
description: From your first optimization problem to methods, solvers and deployment.
text: LLM4OM turns a business problem and its data into an optimization model, then uses a solver to compute a concrete plan. Describe requirements in natural language, inspect the model and actual values, and recalculate when conditions change. Where to begin Follow Your first plan for a complete example. If you do not have access to a running platform, use Install and launch to start one on your computer or server. The product website uses fixed interactive examples; the full platform accepts your own problems and attachments. There are two parallel entry points: Entry point How it works Optimization chat Send a problem and data, then compute and revise plans through conversation Manual modeling workbench Edit the problem, select a configuration and click Start modeling If the problem is still unclear, use requirements chat to prepare an editable draft first. The workbench's lower-left controls switch Chinese/English and light, dark or system appearance. Smaller screens use tabs for the main content and assistant; desktop dividers resize the workspace. What a run produces A run saves the problem, attachments, mathematical model, solver code, actual solver result and intermediate steps. Discuss the result, revise requirements, or export Excel, CSV and Markdown reports. An optimal status applies to the mathematical model the solver actually computed. Before using a plan, check that its objective, constraints, data and variable meanings match the business problem. See Review and export results . Continue by task For everyday use, follow the user guides from data preparation to scenario comparison . For modeling strategies, read Modeling methods . Each method has its own workflow and current parameters. For computation tools, read Libraries and solvers for capabilities, backends and license requirements. For shared use, read Team deployment and Configuration and backups .

title: Your first plan
description: Build, solve and revise a small production plan.
text: This example uses two products and two resources to walk through describing a problem, solving it, checking the plan and changing a requirement. 1. Prepare the platform Open your team's platform address, or install and launch a local service. If the server has no default LLM, open LLM presets at the lower left and add a provider, model ID and key. See Configure LLM presets . 2. Enter a complete problem Open Optimization chat and send this problem. You can also paste it into the manual workbench. A factory makes products A and B in nonnegative integer quantities. Each A earns CNY 3 and uses 2 cutting units and 1 processing unit. Each B earns CNY 2 and uses 1 cutting unit and 2 processing units. There are 8 units of each resource. How much of each product should we make to maximize total profit? In the manual workbench, select Direct, Pyomo and the AUTO backend, then click Start modeling. These are also the defaults in Optimization chat. Computation uses your configured LLM and an actual solver. 3. Check the plan The integer model has an optimum of 3 units of A, 2 units of B and CNY 13 profit . It uses 8 cutting units and 7 processing units. Check the integer domains, both resource constraints and the profit coefficients. Open Solution to inspect quantities and Formulation to inspect the model. Export Excel downloads the full result. 4. Change a requirement Send “Produce at least 3 units of B, keeping all other conditions unchanged. Recalculate.” You can also click Adjust conditions on the result page. The revised optimum is CNY 12 . The original plan remains available for comparison. Use business scenario comparison to test several requirements together, or discuss the plan to understand a result.

title: Install and launch
description: Start the platform with Docker Compose or a local Python environment.
text: If your team already provides a platform address, open it in your browser. To run your own service, Docker Compose provides the shortest setup. Use Docker Compose Install Docker with Compose v2.24 or later. The server does not need a separate Python, uv or Node.js installation. git clone https://github.com/Fangziyang0910/LLM4OM.git cd LLM4OM cp .env.example . env chmod 600 . env Edit .env with the actual provider, endpoint, model ID and API key. See Configure LLM presets for the fields. Then start the service: docker compose up -d --build Open http://localhost:8767 . The first build downloads dependencies and creates the solver sandbox image. Wait for the service to finish starting before opening the workbench. Use a local Python environment Install Python 3.11–3.13, uv and Docker. In your cloned repository, run: uv sync --all-extras uv run llm4om build-worker uv run llm4om serve --workspace runs/web --port 8767 The repository includes the built workbench, so regular use does not require Node.js. This Python service still solves in Docker sandboxes. The --sandbox local option executes generated code on the host and is intended for development. After launch Check that an LLM preset is available, then follow Your first plan to test the complete workflow. Devices on the same network can use the server's IP address and port. See Team deployment for shared use, access controls and HTTPS. GitHub Pages hosts the product website and this documentation. The full platform's LLM calls, Python service and solvers run separately.

title: How modeling works
description: Understand methods, LLMs, modeling libraries, solvers and saved runs.
text: A run depends on the problem, modeling method, LLM and solver environment. Their separate roles help explain both configuration choices and results. From problem to plan Natural-language problem + data ↓ A modeling method organizes LLM calls ↓ Mathematical model + Python code ↓ The sandbox executes code; a backend solves the model ↓ Status, objective, decisions and recorded steps Four distinct choices Choice What it determines Examples Modeling method How a model is generated, checked and repaired Direct, TriVAL, BIND LLM preset Which language model reasons and generates code Your configured model service and model ID Modeling library Which Python interface expresses the model Pyomo, CPMpy, CVXPY Solver backend Which engine computes the solution HiGHS, CP-SAT, Gurobi, Ipopt Changing the LLM does not directly change the solver. Choosing another library does not automatically broaden a method's problem scope. See the method guide and solver guide . What a run saves Each run fixes its problem, attachments, configuration, steps, formulation, code and actual result. A revision creates a separate run for comparison. Deleting a preset or changing server configuration later does not rewrite saved runs. Read the status correctly optimal : the solver established optimality for the current model. feasible : a solution exists, possibly without proof of optimality. locally_optimal : a local optimization conclusion, often for nonlinear models. infeasible : the current model is infeasible; conflict evidence may be available. Execution failure: code, dependencies, interfaces or limits prevented completion. Solver status and business-model correctness are separate judgments. If method validation fails even though a solver reports optimality, read the failed stage and its feedback first.

title: Chat Agent
description: Describe a problem, compute a plan and make changes through conversation.
text: The Chat Agent appears as Optimization chat in the sidebar. It combines requirements, actual modeling, result discussion and revisions in one ongoing conversation. Start with a message Send a complete problem or discuss an initial idea. General questions, writing, code explanation and arithmetic do not automatically start optimization. When you need a plan, describe the decisions, objective and requirements, then attach any data. Use the attached data to schedule next week's staff. At least 3 people must work each day; each person works at most 5 days. A supervisor must work on weekends. Minimize total staffing cost. The assistant asks for information that matters to the next step. Once the problem is clear, it runs the full modeling workflow, generates a formulation and code, and solves the model. Follow computation and inspect the plan The conversation shows actual stages and links to saved plans. On desktop, the adjacent modeling workspace shows the process, formulation, code and results. Open the full run page to export Excel. Drag the divider, or focus it with Tab and use the arrow keys, to resize the panels. Defaults are Direct, Pyomo and AUTO. Specify a method, library or backend in your message, or fix a method and library through Modeling preferences beside the input. For example: “Use BIND to read this JSON and model it with Pyomo.” Ask questions or change requirements Your message What happens “Why are these two people assigned to Tuesday?” The assistant reads and explains the existing model and result “Calculate weekend costs for this plan.” It calculates from actual decisions without solving again “Tuesday needs at least 4 people. Keep everything else and recalculate.” It creates a revised problem and solves a new model “Compare budgets of 1000 and 1200.” It computes scenarios from the same baseline A single new plan becomes the current plan for later discussion. Say “Return to the original plan without recalculating” or “Use the second plan from now on” to select a baseline. Merely viewing a historical plan does not change it. Data, search and recovery Click attachments to inspect or edit them. Changes affect later models. Explicitly request a new model to use updated data; saved plans retain their own inputs. Enable web search when public information is useful and expand the sources. Confirm suggested business rules before using them in computation. The DeepSeek thinking toggle controls the conversation turn; modeling tools retain their run preset. Enter sends; Shift+Enter inserts a line break. Stop or retry a turn as needed. Refresh reconnects to active runs. Saved plans remain available if the final text reply fails, and deleting a conversation does not delete its separately saved plans.

headings.label: Follow computation and inspect the plan

title: Clarify requirements
description: Turn an initial idea into an editable problem statement and data.
text: Requirements chat helps when you do not yet have a complete problem statement. It organizes goals, rules, data and open questions into a draft you can edit. Open it and describe the idea On the manual modeling home page, choose Prepare requirements through chat. Existing text and attachments are carried over, or you can start empty. Describe the decision first: “I need to allocate inventory across three warehouses, but I am unsure what data to prepare.” The assistant updates the draft and asks about information that matters to the problem. The main editor keeps the draft visible, with the assistant beside it on desktop and a tab switch on smaller screens. Review and edit the draft Edit quantities, units, indices and mandatory requirements directly. Manual edits save when you leave the editor, or through Save draft. Pending edits are saved before the next message or modeling handoff. Inspect and edit attachments as needed. Web search can help find public information; expand and check its sources. Confirm suggested rules before treating them as fixed requirements. Hand it to a modeling method Once the draft is ready, select the run configuration and click Start modeling. You can also choose Use for modeling to adopt the draft and close the assistant. The method receives the problem text and attachments, rather than the conversation itself. The requirements assistant does not start solving on its own. Review unresolved questions before handoff so tentative requirements are not mistaken for confirmed ones. How it differs from Optimization chat Optimization chat can call modeling tools, save plans and revise them within a conversation. Requirements chat focuses on an editable problem statement for users who want to review it before starting a run. Resume the conversation from history; deleting it does not delete modeling runs already created from it.

headings.label: Open it and describe the idea
Hand it to a modeling method
How it differs from Optimization chat

title: Upload and edit data
description: Review spreadsheets, fields and units before computing with the full data.
text: Data and the problem statement together form the modeling input. Explain each field and its units, especially the relationships between costs, times, quantities and identifiers. Supported files Upload CSV, TSV, JSON, text or Excel .xlsx workbooks. Each Excel worksheet becomes a separate CSV attachment. Ordinary attachments have a 2 MB per-file limit; converted worksheets are used as separate data files. A production table could contain: Product,Profit (CNY),Cutting units,Processing units A,3,2,1 B,2,1,2 State resource capacities and variable domains in the problem text. The table supplies parameters; the description explains how to use them. Inspect and edit Click an attachment name to open the editor. CSV and TSV support cell and column-name editing. JSON and text use the source editor. Tables show 50 rows per page while pagination and saving retain the entire dataset. Use source editing for more than 50 columns. Values retain their original text, so identifier 001 does not silently become 1 . Fix incomplete CSV quotes or invalid JSON before saving. Save data applies edits; Cancel keeps the original attachment. How complete data reaches computation Ordinary methods may see an attachment preview in their prompts. Generated code reads the full content through build_model(data) . BIND passes JSON/CSV structure to the LLM and parses the complete data during execution, which is useful for long datasets. After changing data Editing draft or chat attachments affects later computation. Saved plans retain their original inputs. Explicitly request a new model or start another run to use updated attachments, then check the files recorded with the new problem.

title: Configure a run
description: Select a method, modeling library, solver backend and LLM preset.
text: The manual workbench lets you review a complete problem and configuration before starting computation. Optimization chat can also specify these choices; see Chat Agent . Select four settings Open View run settings or Adjust configuration above the problem. Setting What to consider Modeling method Generation, validation and repair workflow; see Methods Modeling library Its ability to express the variables, objective and constraints; see Libraries and solvers Solver backend An installed engine compatible with the model; AUTO is the default LLM preset The language model service called during the run Method parameters are fixed in deployment presets, rather than editable per-run form fields. The run records the actual parameter snapshot for later inspection. Review the problem and start Check decisions, objective direction, constraints, units, integer or continuous domains and attachment fields. Switch between Markdown editing and preview. Use \(...\) , \[...\] or $$...$$ for formulas in a problem statement; a single $ in a price remains text. Click Done to close the settings, then Start modeling, or press Ctrl+Enter / Cmd+Enter. Wait for attachments to finish loading before starting. Follow progress The server runs the computation while the page shows actual steps. Closing the browser does not cancel a background run. Reopening retrieves its process and current progress. Stopping preserves saved steps, but does not imply that a method can resume from the interrupted node. Handle incompatible settings A library's interfaces do not imply that every backend can solve every model. Integer variables, for example, require an integer-capable backend. An explicitly selected backend is not silently replaced after failure. Read the full error and adjust configuration or model expression rather than using a continuous relaxation by mistake.

title: Review and export results
description: Inspect decisions, the model and solver status, then export the full plan.
text: After a run, read the solver status, objective and concrete decisions, then check that the formulation represents the original problem. The result page retains the model, code, inputs, data and modeling process. Read the actual decisions The result explanation adds business labels and units. Table values come directly from the solver; the LLM supplies labels and text. Explanation reads at most 100 nonzero variables, or the first 100 for an all-zero solution. The full variables remain available for expansion, search and export. Two-dimensional variables can appear as matrices. When a method revises the model or code, inspect versions and compare with the previous one. Failure of the explanation call does not remove the solver result. Interpret the status Status or situation How to read it Optimal Optimality applies to this model; still check its match to the problem Feasible, or timed out with a solution Inspect the actual solution; optimality may be unproven Locally optimal Retain its local meaning; see CasADi Infeasible See Infeasibility ; this is not an executable plan Method validation failed Read the failed stage and feedback even if the solver has a result If new code fails before execution, the page does not attach the preceding version's result to it. Earlier results remain visible in the process steps. Choose an export Excel : the plan sheet includes business labels, all variable values and units. A problem sheet retains the statement, revisions, attachment names, configuration and links. Zero values are included, regardless of the page's display range. CSV : download complete variable values for further computation or checks. Markdown report : problem, settings, result, model, code and notes, with at most 500 nonzero variables and an explicit range notice. Optimal, feasible, locally optimal and timed-out runs with an actual solution can export Excel. Infeasible, unbounded and failed runs are not exported as executable plans. An export is a snapshot; editing Excel does not solve the model again. Continue with the plan Use Discuss plan, Adjust conditions or Business scenario comparison below the result. Explain the existing result first, then specify requirements to change, keeping a clear computation baseline.

title: Discuss a saved plan
description: Explain decisions, calculate totals and continue from the current plan.
text: Choose Discuss plan on a result page to ask about that run's problem, formulation and actual values. The assistant reads a fixed result; ordinary explanation does not solve again. Questions to ask Explain the shipment quantities from each warehouse. Which resource limits further production? Point to the model evidence. Calculate total shipping cost and remaining inventory for this plan. Totals, resource balances and ratios can use actual decision values directly. A Calculation check card shows the computed value; expand it to inspect the expression and number of variables read. This tool can access complete variables beyond the text explanation's display range. When you need a new plan State the change explicitly: “Increase the budget to 1200, keep all other conditions and recalculate.” The assistant inherits the baseline's method, LLM preset, library, backend and attachments, prepares a new problem and executes the full workflow. The conversational reply can use a separately selected preset. This does not rewrite the baseline's saved modeling configuration. Each new plan is saved independently and can be opened for complete inspection and export. Current and historical plans The assistant identifies the Current discussion plan. Viewing history changes what you see, rather than the baseline for later computation. Explicitly say “Return to the original plan” or identify another saved plan to switch it. A single new plan becomes current. Multiple scenarios are calculated from the same baseline, leaving the current plan unchanged. Stop, refresh and retry Enter sends and Shift+Enter inserts a line break. Stop or retry as needed; conversations remain available after refresh. If the final reply fails, saved results can still be opened and retries read the completed plans. Deleting the conversation does not delete those independent runs.

headings.label: When you need a new plan

title: Revise requirements
description: Change a requirement while keeping the original plan for comparison.
text: Requirement revision changes one or more conditions of an existing problem and computes a new plan. The original problem, configuration and result remain available. Start a revision Click Adjust conditions on the result page. State what changes and what stays fixed: Produce at least 3 units of B. Keep all other conditions unchanged. Generate new plan first prepares a complete revised problem. It then inherits the original method, LLM preset, library, backend and attachments, and solves again. You can make the same request through plan chat . Read the comparison The new run shows both objectives, decision changes and problem-text differences. In the production example, original profit is CNY 13; requiring at least 3 units of B changes the optimum to CNY 12. The baseline comes from a checkpoint saved when revision starts. Rerunning the original thread later does not rewrite that comparison. Variables match by name; added or missing variables are identified rather than treated as zero. Choose a baseline for later changes In conversation, a single new plan becomes current and later revisions start from it. Say “Start from the original plan” to return to the original requirements. Use business scenarios for multiple independent changes. What to check Review the new problem to ensure it changes only the intended requirements. If objective meaning or units change, interpret each objective in its own business context rather than comparing numbers alone. Check recorded data after changing attachments. Deleting the original run removes its baseline checkpoint, while the new run remains separately saved.

headings.label: Choose a baseline for later changes

title: Compare business scenarios
description: Compare demand or resource changes from one fixed baseline.
text: Business scenario comparison asks how one original plan changes under several independent conditions. Each scenario is generated and solved from the same baseline, so one scenario's change does not carry into the next. Create scenarios Choose Business scenario comparison below the original run and enter 2–6 names and changes. For the production example: Scenario Change At least 3 of B Produce at least 3 units of B; keep everything else unchanged At least 4 of B Produce at least 4 units of B; keep everything else unchanged Click Calculate and compare. Each scenario inherits the same original problem, attachments and settings. You can also request several explicit scenarios in Optimization chat or plan chat. Read the actual differences The original example earns CNY 13. These two scenarios have optima of CNY 12 and CNY 8. The comparison shows actual statuses, objectives, units and key decisions. Open an individual plan to inspect its complete model and variables. The comparison prioritizes the first 20 changed variables with matching names; each run retains all values. Missing variables appear as — . Objectives with different meanings or units are not directly ranked. Save and continue Each scenario is an independent run and the original remains a fixed baseline. Creating several scenarios in chat does not switch the current discussion plan. Explicitly select a scenario to continue from it. If some scenarios fail to start or save, completed runs remain available. Check which scenarios actually finished before retrying the remainder. A missing result does not mean infeasibility.

title: Compare methods and LLMs
description: Run different methods or LLMs on the same problem and inspect the results.
text: Method comparison holds the problem fixed and compares actual outputs from different modeling methods or LLM presets. Scenario comparison instead changes business requirements. Start a comparison In the manual workbench, open Run settings, enable Compare and select multiple methods or LLM presets, up to 12 runs. Confirm the problem, attachments, library and backend before starting. Each item executes independently and retains its own formulation, code, steps and solver result. Open a row in the comparison table to inspect that run. Read the comparison table Information What it helps explain Status and objective Whether solving completed and whether model objectives agree Duration Actual execution time, excluding queue time LLM calls and tokens The method's call cost on this problem Formulation, code and steps Modeling choices or errors behind numerical differences Equal objective values do not imply identical or correct models. When values differ, inspect domains, objective direction, constraints and data binding before attributing the difference to a method. Keep comparison conditions clear For method comparisons, hold the problem, attachments, LLM preset, library and backend fixed where possible. For LLM comparisons, fix the method and solving environment. Save configurations and reports, including actual preset parameters rather than only method names. A single problem helps explain specific behavior. Measuring overall modeling ability requires a sourced problem set, reference answers and consistent criteria. Side-by-side display alone does not establish a general accuracy result.

title: Understand infeasibility
description: Use solver evidence to inspect requirements that cannot hold together.
text: Infeasibility means the current model's requirements cannot all hold together. When concrete solver evidence is available, the platform maps conflicting constraints to business requirements so you can decide what to change. When diagnosis is available Current paths include Gurobi IIS for linear models and MUS for CPMpy models. CVXPY does not provide this diagnosis here. An infeasible status does not necessarily include an explainable conflict set. When evidence exists, the result page shows Why infeasible. Expand the corresponding constraints to inspect the model conditions behind each explanation. A concrete example Each A uses 2 cutting units; total cutting capacity is 8. Additional requirement: produce at least 5 units of A. These requirements conflict: 5 units of A alone need 10 cutting units. First check that the model accurately reflects the business rules, then decide whether to add capacity or change the production requirement. Try a revision The platform offers at most one evidence-based candidate change. It has not been validated by another solve and does not directly alter the original constraints. Try this adjustment fills the revision text. Review or edit it, then compute a new plan to test it. The original problem and result remain saved. Feedback Repair reads available diagnosis to check modeling errors. Research methods retain their own feedback workflows. Infeasibility can be a correct result; fixed requirements should not be relaxed merely to obtain a solution. When no diagnosis is available The platform does not produce a definite conflict explanation when diagnosis fails, no evidence is supplied or the result is only locally infeasible. Read the original error and check units, bounds and configuration. Large-model Gurobi diagnosis also requires a suitable license. See CasADi for local-status semantics.

title: History, tags and reports
description: Find related plans, record conclusions and export reports.
text: History preserves each run's problem, data, configuration and result so you can recover originals, compare revisions and record conclusions. Find related records The sidebar groups requirements chats, runs, revisions and comparisons by their recorded problem origin. Expand Related records to inspect them. Identical titles do not automatically mean the same problem. Older records without origin information remain separate. History loads 100 records at a time. Use Load earlier runs to continue. Text and tag filters apply to the loaded records, with that range shown in the interface. Notes, tags and reports On a run page, choose More actions → Notes and tags to record conclusions and categories. Search for #tag in the sidebar. Export report (Markdown) saves the problem, settings, result, model, code and notes. Runs and comparisons have stable links for people with access to the same platform. See Results for complete Excel and CSV exports. Rerun and delete Run again uses the same problem and settings. Edit and run returns inputs to the editor. If the original preset was deleted, select another preset. Deleting an independent record does not cascade to other related runs; deleting an original removes its associated comparison baseline. Storage and shared access Use the same workspace to retain presets and history across normal server restarts. Stopped runs retain saved steps, without guaranteeing that a method can resume from the interrupted point. The workbench has no built-in login or user-level permissions. People who can access the service can view and manage shared records. Control access through networking or a reverse proxy and follow the backup guide .

title: Examples and benchmarks
description: Start from built-in examples and explore public benchmark problems.
text: Built-in examples support a first walkthrough. Public benchmarks help you explore problem descriptions and select modeling cases for further inspection. Begin with a small example The home page offers sample problems that you can load into the editor and run with your chosen method and solver environment. Start with the production plan to check integer domains, two resource constraints and the objective before using your own data. The product website's three interactive examples compute fixed small problems in the browser to explain the interaction. Runs in the full platform use your configured LLM and an actual solver. Public benchmark coverage The example library contains 9 groups and 2,033 problem statements: Benchmark Problems Benchmark Problems NL4Opt 205 IndustryOR 99 NL4LP 178 ComplexOR 18 MAMO Easy 642 OptiBench 403 MAMO Complex 210 OptMATH 128 NL4COP 150 Open Example library, read a problem and load it into the editor. The statements come from the OPT-Agent collection and do not include answers. See the source and license notes . Use benchmarks for checks Some problems exceed LP/MILP scope. Check the method scope and solver capabilities first. Loading a problem does not provide a reference answer or automatic scoring. For evaluation, separately retain sources, reference solutions, run configurations and judgment criteria.

title: Configure LLM presets
description: Connect model services and manage fixed presets and provider parameters.
text: An LLM preset fixes a provider, endpoint, model ID, key and request parameters. Modeling and conversations select a preset rather than accepting a fresh key on each run. Add a preset Open LLM presets at the lower left. Select the provider, enter its model ID, key and required endpoint, then save. A preset name controls display only; API requests use the model ID. Supported providers include OpenAI, Gemini, Kimi, GLM, OpenRouter, Bailian, DeepSeek, Anthropic and OpenAI-compatible services. Failed saves retain the form. For 401 errors, check the key; for 404, check the endpoint, protocol and model ID. To change fixed parameters, delete and recreate the preset. The new preset receives a new ID. Server default preset Set these fields in .env to provide the default preset with ID env : LLM4OM_LLM_PROVIDER=openai_compatible LLM4OM_LLM_BASE_URL=https://api.example.com/v1 LLM4OM_LLM_MODEL=your-model-id LLM4OM_LLM_API_KEY=your-api-key LLM4OM_LLM_NAME=Team model Replace these placeholders with actual service details. Only the server configuration can change this default; the UI cannot delete it. Keys stay in private server configuration, outside run records and the generated-code environment. Provider-specific parameters TriVAL's structured output requires forced tool selection. With DeepSeek, disable thinking in the extra request body: { "thinking" : { "type" : "disabled" } } The DeepSeek thinking toggle in chat controls that reply; modeling tools still use the run preset. OpenRouter supports dedicated reasoning parameters, while unsupported fields produce an error. Extra parameters cannot replace existing model, key or temperature fields, or recording callbacks. Usage and history The preset dialog shows daily usage. The service can enforce daily token limits; see Configuration and usage . Deleting a preset leaves saved results intact. Rerunning an old record requires an available preset.

title: Choose a modeling method
description: Compare the workflows, scope and configuration of 13 methods.
text: A modeling method determines how the LLM builds the formulation and code, and when it validates, debugs or searches further. Configure it separately from the LLM preset, library and solver backend. Choose by workflow Start with Direct for a first run. Consider Feedback Repair when you want a post-solve review. Use the table to explore specific mechanisms; it groups workflows rather than ranking accuracy. Method Main workflow Explicit problem scope Direct One generation of formulation and code Determined jointly by prompts, library and backend Feedback Repair Generate, solve, review against the problem and repair As above TriVAL Semantic, formulation and code validation As above OptiMUS 0.3 Extract components, formulate, assemble and debug LP/MILP Chain-of-Experts Sequential expert selection and reduction LP/MILP OptiTree Type-tree matching, guidance retrieval and code inspection LP/MILP OR-LLM-Agent Formulation, code, execution and rechecks LP/MILP ORThought Reasoning path, formulation, code and execution debugging Determined jointly by prompts, library and backend LLMOPT Five-part formulation and self-correction As above AutoFormulation Component tree, MCTS and model ranking LP/MILP SAC-Opt Semantic anchors, backtranslation and selective repair LP/MILP BIND Data structure, full-data binding and execution repair Determined jointly by prompts, library and backend OptiMind Public type hints and multi-turn feedback As above Configure and compare Select a method in Run settings or name it in a Chat Agent request. All 13 built-in methods accept nine libraries, but the library's expression capabilities, the backend's solving capabilities and the method's own scope must all fit the problem. Deployment presets fix method parameters. Each method page generates its parameter table from current code. The UI, CLI and Python API do not accept per-run parameter changes; actual snapshots are saved with the run. Method comparison helps inspect behavior while keeping inputs and environment fixed. What a research method means here Ports retain core orchestration, prompts and stopping conditions, with documented code-contract and execution adaptations. SAC-Opt is independently implemented. BIND and OptiMind have explicit public-scope and deployment adaptations. Their individual pages explain these distinctions. Methods use your configured LLM. Integrating an inference workflow does not automatically deploy a paper's trained model or reproduce its benchmark results. Inspect the actual model, parameters, steps and result for each run.

headings.label: What a research method means here

title: Direct
description: Generate the mathematical model and solver code in one LLM call.
text: Direct generates the formulation and complete solver code in one LLM call. The platform then executes the code and solves the model. It is the default method in Optimization chat. Workflow Problem and attachments → formulation and code → format check → solve The prompt asks for explicit variable domains, indices, units, objective direction, data sources and constraints. Missing formulation or code produces a failure rather than sending empty code to the solver. How to use it Choose Direct in Run settings or use the default Optimization chat configuration. Select a library and backend that can express and solve the problem. Its short call sequence makes it a useful starting point for inspecting a formulation. Attachment previews may omit rows. Generated code should read the complete attachment through build_model(data) . Consider BIND for structured-data binding on longer inputs. What to inspect Check domains, objective coefficients, capacities and actual decisions. Direct has no post-solve semantic review loop; choose Feedback Repair for that stage. Valid infeasible or unbounded statuses are solver results, rather than evidence that execution never occurred. Implementation source Direct is maintained by LLM4OM. It shares generation prompts and a generation node with Feedback Repair, which adds solving, review and bounded repair. Current parameters Parameters come from the deployed method preset. They are saved with each run and cannot be changed per run in the UI, CLI or Python API. Direct has no method-specific preset parameters. Parameter definitions

title: Feedback Repair
description: Review the solved model against the problem and repair specific errors.
text: Feedback Repair adds post-solve review to Direct generation. It checks the objective, domains, constraints and data binding against the original problem, then repairs specific formulation or code errors. Workflow Generate → solve → review against the problem → finish ↑ format, execution or modeling issue ↓ └──────────────── repair from feedback ──────────┘ Review still checks the problem meaning when the solver reports optimality. Available conflict diagnosis also informs review. Without repairs, the method itself uses two LLM calls and one solve; later result explanation is additional. How to use it Select Feedback Repair in Run settings for a workflow that reviews problem meaning after computation. Provide clear requirements and data, and choose a compatible library and backend. Format, execution and modeling corrections share a limit of three repairs. A time limit, a merely feasible result or an objective-free satisfaction problem is not by itself a reason to change the model. Read failures and infeasibility A correctly infeasible or unbounded model can finish without relaxing requirements to obtain a solution. Unresolved review or an unparsable reply preserves completed artifacts and reports failure. If later generation is incomplete, the last actually solved model and result remain traceable. Implementation source This method is maintained by LLM4OM. Review is an additional check rather than a correctness proof. It does not introduce SAC-Opt's semantic anchors or OptiMind's specialized hint library. Current parameters Parameters come from the deployed method preset. They are saved with each run and cannot be changed per run in the UI, CLI or Python API. Parameter Value max_repairs 3 Parameter definitions

title: TriVAL
description: Validate semantics, formulation and code, with revisions across stages.
text: TriVAL separates validation into semantics, mathematical formulation and code. Each stage constructs, validates and revises its output. Code issues can send the process back to formulation. Workflow Semantic facts and validation → formulation and validation → code, execution and validation ↑ ↓ └──── revise when needed ──────┘ The stages distinguish understanding the problem, expressing it mathematically and implementing it in code. Intermediate artifacts and feedback appear in the process view. How to use it Select TriVAL with a library and backend suitable for the problem. It supports workflows where you want to inspect stage-by-stage judgments as well as the final numbers. With DeepSeek, disable thinking in the run preset because structured output requires forced tool selection. See LLM presets . What to inspect Read the semantic facts, formulation, code and validation feedback. Reaching a validation limit does not mean a stage passed. The platform reports unresolved stages and keeps actual artifacts and solver results. An optimal solver status does not override method-validation failure. Source and adaptation The core graph, nodes, prompts and loops come from the pinned SCUT-EIPI/TriVAL source . The platform supplies LLMs and sandboxes, adapting code to return native models through build_model(data) . Original documentation linked below records the detailed adaptations. Current parameters Parameters come from the deployed method preset. They are saved with each run and cannot be changed per run in the UI, CLI or Python API. Parameter Value max_validations 5 max_code_executions 20 Parameter definitions

title: OptiMUS 0.3
description: Extract parameters, objectives and constraints, then assemble component code.
text: OptiMUS 0.3 decomposes a problem into parameters, objective and constraints. It builds expressions and code component by component, then assembles and executes them. Its platform ID is optimus . Workflow Parameters → objective and constraints → constraint checks → formulation → component code → assembly → execution → debugging if needed Constraint extraction includes redundancy and confidence checks. Components use the selected library and are assembled into the complete platform function. How to use it Select OptiMUS 0.3 to inspect how individual objectives and constraints are formed. It retains LP/MILP scope. Supply parameter values explicitly in the statement or attachments; an upstream-format params.json can also be used. All nine libraries are available, without converting nonlinear requirements to linear ones or relaxing variable domains to fit a library. Process and stopping behavior Inspect parameter values, individual constraint expressions, the objective and assembled code. Execution errors trigger bounded debugging. The upstream workflow treats optimal status as debugging success, so infeasible or unbounded models may also enter debugging. This differs from Feedback Repair's stopping rules. Source and adaptation The workflow and prompts follow the pinned OptiMUS v0.3 source and v0.3 paper . The platform removes interactive input, does not enable upstream RAG, and adapts execution and code contracts to the chosen library and sandbox. Current parameters Parameters come from the deployed method preset. They are saved with each run and cannot be changed per run in the UI, CLI or Python API. Parameter Value temperature 1 max_debug_tries 3 Parameter definitions

title: Chain-of-Experts
description: A conductor selects experts in sequence before a reducer produces the model.
text: Chain-of-Experts (CoE) asks experts to comment in sequence, then uses a reducer to produce the formulation and code. A conductor selects the next expert from the discussion so far. Workflow Start trial → conductor selects expert → expert comments → continue or reduce → model and code The upstream design provides seven expert roles. The platform retains their prompts, conductor and reducer, rather than replacing the sequence with a parallel vote. How to use it Select Chain-of-Experts for LP/MILP problems to inspect how interpretation, modeling and code advice are combined. Each trial starts with an empty comment pool. The default allows up to three collaborating experts and disables reflection. Reflection is a deployment preset, not a per-message toggle. When enabled, an execution error triggers responsibility analysis from the last expert backwards before further trials. What to inspect Inspect expert selection, individual comments and the final model. Expert opinions are not solver results; numerical values come from actual sandbox computation. With reflection disabled by default, multiple experts do not imply automatic multi-round repair on every run. Source and adaptation The workflow and prompts follow the pinned Chain-of-Experts source . The platform supplies the complete shared library contract and executes code in the sandbox. Reflection reads actual solver feedback rather than generating extra test inputs. Current parameters Parameters come from the deployed method preset. They are saved with each run and cannot be changed per run in the UI, CLI or Python API. Parameter Value temperature 0 max_collaborate_nums 3 enable_reflection false max_trials 3 Parameter definitions

title: OptiTree
description: Match a problem type in a tree, retrieve guidance and generate code.
text: OptiTree matches a problem down a type tree, retrieves guidance from the matched node and generates code. Its classification retains mixed-integer programming as the root scope. Workflow Classify from the root → match child types → retrieve guidance → reason and generate code → execute → inspect errors The deepest matched entry guides reasoning. If code cannot run, an inspector revises it using actual sandbox feedback within the inspection limit. How to use it Select OptiTree and submit a clear LP/MILP problem to inspect how classification and retrieved guidance affect modeling. The upstream type tree and templates are distributed with the platform; you do not need to build a separate library. Changing the modeling library changes the code contract, rather than the tree's mathematical scope. What to inspect Inspect the classification path, retrieved entry, reasoning, formulation and code. If classification names an absent type, omits judgment fields or loops back to a visited node, the platform stops at the current node. Retrieved guidance still needs to be checked against the actual problem. Source and adaptation See the pinned OptiTree source and paper . Classification, reasoning and inspection prompts and the original tree are retained. Code requests are adapted to return native models for sandbox solving. Current parameters Parameters come from the deployed method preset. They are saved with each run and cannot be changed per run in the UI, CLI or Python API. Parameter Value temperature 0 max_inspections 4 Parameter definitions

title: OR-LLM-Agent
description: Build the formulation first, then generate, execute and recheck code.
text: OR-LLM-Agent writes a mathematical formulation before generating code and repairing execution errors. After the main round, it performs an infeasibility check or model recheck. Workflow Formulation → code → execution → error repair → result-dependent infeasibility check or recheck The main round, infeasibility check and recheck use their separate attempts preset budgets rather than an unbounded retry loop. How to use it Select OR-LLM-Agent for LP/MILP problems when you want to inspect a standalone formulation followed by execution feedback and rechecks. Agent here names the modeling workflow. The website's Chat Agent is the conversational entry point that can call different methods. Match final code to execution Repair conversations use a copy, with only the final code returned to the main conversation. Upstream may leave its last repair unexecuted. The platform preserves such code as an intermediate artifact and associates final numerical results with the last actually executed code. Check versions together with execution steps. Source and adaptation The core follows the pinned OR-LLM-Agent source . Prompts and recovery routes are retained, with Gurobi-specific code requests replaced by the selected library contract and execution moved to the sandbox. Current parameters Parameters come from the deployed method preset. They are saved with each run and cannot be changed per run in the UI, CLI or Python API. Parameter Value temperature 0.2 attempts {"main":3,"infeasible":1,"recheck":2} Parameter definitions

title: ORThought
description: Write a reasoning path, formulation and code, then debug execution errors.
text: ORThought writes a reasoning path, formulation and code in the order of an expert modeling workflow. If execution fails, it debugs using the problem, formulation and error. Workflow Understand objective, variables and constraints → reasoning path → formulation and code → execute → debug code if needed The reasoning path is saved as the solution_path artifact. It makes the interpretation and organization of the model visible for inspecting where constraints came from. How to use it Select ORThought with a library and backend suitable for the problem. Check whether the reasoning identifies the decisions, objective direction and requirements before inspecting expressions and code. Execution errors trigger bounded debugging. Code that executes but produces an infeasible model does not automatically enter that debugging loop. Inspect platform evidence separately when you need to understand infeasibility. Integrated scope The platform integrates the upstream formalized modeling mode and solve agent. It does not include the paper's multi-agent comparison or LogiOR dataset. Code extraction is adapted so a short valid build_model(data) function is not rejected by the upstream length threshold. Source See the pinned ORThought source and paper . The source has no declared license; the project records the prompts for research reproduction in NOTICE . Current parameters Parameters come from the deployed method preset. They are saved with each run and cannot be changed per run in the UI, CLI or Python API. Parameter Value temperature 0 debug_max_try 3 Parameter definitions

title: LLMOPT
description: Construct a five-part formulation and route corrections to the affected stage.
text: LLMOPT builds a five-part formulation before generating code. Self-correction judges the formulation and code separately and routes repairs to the relevant stage. Workflow Sets, parameters, variables, objective, constraints → code → execute → self-correct ↑ formulation error ↓ code error └── redefine the model rewrite code A formulation error returns to definition and then code generation. A code-only error returns to code generation. The result comes from actual execution, with re-solves limited by the preset. How to use it Select LLMOPT when you want to inspect problem structure separately from its code mapping. Check all five sections, parameter sources and coverage of the original requirements. The platform preserves correspondence between executed code and its result. New code that fails before execution does not inherit the previous version's solution. Workflow versus trained model The research includes a fine-tuned and aligned model. The platform integrates the test-time five-part and self-correction workflow, using your selected preset. It does not automatically download the paper's model. To use released weights, deploy a compatible model service and add its preset. Source and adaptation Prompts follow the pinned LLMOPT source ; the correction loop follows the paper . Upstream did not publish that loop's code, so routing decisions are documented in the original adaptation notes. Prompts use the chosen library and platform code contract. Research-reproduction license notes appear in the project NOTICE. Current parameters Parameters come from the deployed method preset. They are saved with each run and cannot be changed per run in the UI, CLI or Python API. Parameter Value max_resolves 12 Parameter definitions

title: AutoFormulation
description: Search candidate components and rank complete models with MCTS and comparisons.
text: AutoFormulation searches multiple candidate models. It builds a component tree, uses Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) to explore complete models, and ranks them with pairwise comparisons. Workflow Parameters → decision variables → objective → equalities → inequalities Sample, check execution, remove equivalents and rank at each level ↓ MCTS rollouts → complete-model comparisons → select a solved model Candidate components run check scripts. Equivalence uses LLM grouping or symbolic scripts. Relative comparisons between complete models produce search rewards that propagate through the tree. Initial solved models form comparison baselines. Later models are compared in both directions against them, with win rates as rewards. UCT balances established high-scoring paths against less-explored paths, and Bradley–Terry ranking selects a solved model at the end. How to use it Select AutoFormulation for LP/MILP research workflows where candidate search is useful to inspect. State parameters, indices, domains and units explicitly so component assembly remains consistent. Its default budget is substantially larger than single-generation methods and can involve many LLM responses and sandbox checks. Inspect current parameters and deployment limits before a full run. Parameters are changed in deployment code, rather than per run. Inspect the search Review retained and pruned candidates, whether complete models were actually solved, and their rankings. Equivalent candidates may leave a single complete model, without meaningful inter-model comparison. Check the selected model against the problem; LLM ranking does not certify business correctness. Source and adaptation See the pinned AutoFormulator source and ICML 2025 paper . The platform preserves search, uses shared library components and sandboxed scripts, and documents explicit fixes such as the two-candidate comparison direction. Your preset is used rather than automatically reproducing the paper's model and evaluation setup. Current parameters Parameters come from the deployed method preset. They are saved with each run and cannot be changed per run in the UI, CLI or Python API. Parameter Value temperature 1 n_used_gpt 8 n_top 3 n_reward 5 total_rollouts 16 n_dv_unique_gpt 8 n_eval 5 num_warmup 3 w_exp 1 lambda_cte 0.5 max_rollout_attempts 1000 max_comparison_tries 5 limits {"max_llm_calls":20000,"max_solves":1000,"solve_time_limit":60,"run_timeout":21600} Parameter definitions

title: SAC-Opt
description: Extract semantic anchors and selectively repair constraints after backtranslation.
text: SAC-Opt extracts semantic anchors for parameters, variables, objective and constraints. It backtranslates constraint code to text, compares it with the intended constraint, freezes accepted components and repairs only failed ones. Workflow Semantic anchors → component code → backtranslate constraints → compare ↑ ↓ failed └── selective repair ──┘ → assemble → solve → debug execution errors Backtranslation does not read the original constraint. A separate comparison checks consistency, helping locate a specific component rather than rewriting all code. How to use it Select SAC-Opt for LP/MILP workflows that inspect constraints individually. Provide clear business rules and follow the mapping from anchors to constraint components. Shared components support all nine libraries. Complete attachments are read in build_model(data) . Variable domains and bounds must still match the problem and cannot be relaxed merely to fit a library. What to inspect Review anchors, components, backtranslations, individual comparisons and selective repairs. The current loop checks constraints rather than independently validating the objective. If semantic rounds end with unresolved components, the platform keeps actual artifacts and results while reporting semantic-validation failure. Independent implementation and source This implementation follows the SAC-Opt paper and pinned reference . The reference commit has no declared license, so its code and prompts were not copied. The platform batches components and uses its own structured outputs while retaining semantic anchors and selective repair. Current parameters Parameters come from the deployed method preset. They are saved with each run and cannot be changed per run in the UI, CLI or Python API. Parameter Value temperature 0 max_parse_attempts 5 max_semantic_rounds 5 max_executions 3 Parameter definitions

title: BIND
description: Show data structure to the LLM and read complete attachments during execution.
text: BIND shows JSON/CSV structure to the LLM and reads complete data during code execution. It addresses data copying and truncated attachment previews on longer inputs. Workflow Attachment structure → formulation and code → read full attachments and solve ↓ execution or format error regenerate with conversation feedback The LLM receives fields, types, array lengths or CSV row counts. Nested, heterogeneous and nonrectangular JSON structures are described as they are. Full values remain available to execution. Prepare the input Explain fields, units and rules in the problem. For example: “quantity in each order is demand; warehouse_costs is the unit shipping-cost matrix from warehouses to stores.” Upload JSON or CSV, then select BIND and a compatible library. Excel worksheets are converted to CSV by the UI. Without attachments, BIND models directly from the statement. It does not add PDF or image parsing. Interpret the result Check that code binds the intended fields, rows, columns and units. Full-data binding does not replace business-model review. Successful execution with a solver status can finish the workflow. Genuine infeasibility is valid and does not trigger constraint relaxation to match a reference answer. Source and adaptation The integration follows schema offloading and the default agentic path in the pinned Text2Opt-Bench source ; see the paper . User attachments replace benchmark instances. Reference-optimum and model-size scoring dependencies are removed. Outputs include a formulation and build_model(data) , with bounded execution repair. Current parameters Parameters come from the deployed method preset. They are saved with each run and cannot be changed per run in the UI, CLI or Python API. Parameter Value temperature 0 top_p 1 max_rounds 3 Parameter definitions

title: OptiMind
description: Combine public problem-type hints with multi-turn solver feedback.
text: OptiMind combines problem-type hints with multi-turn solver feedback. It matches available public hints, generates and executes a model, then asks the LLM to revise or finish. Workflow Classify type → public hints → generate → solve → feedback ↑ ↓ revise or finish without code └───────────────┘ Feedback is provided even after successful solving. The LLM can return revised code or finish with a code-free answer, retaining the last actually executed model and result. How to use it Select OptiMind with a library and backend suitable for the problem. Traveling-salesman problems may match the public specialized hints. Unmatched problems use general checking guidance. Selecting the method does not automatically load a dedicated trained model. Current public scope The distributed specialized library contains only TravelingSalesman , with six error/hint pairs. The platform does not invent unpublished types or add majority voting by default. It uses one trajectory, with generation limited by the current preset below. If no valid execution exists and a reply lacks code, the method requests code again. Exhausting the limit reports failure rather than treating an unexecuted answer as completion. Inspect explanatory text and actual numerical results separately. Source and adaptation See the pinned OptiGuide/OptiMind source and paper . The platform adds classification restricted to public hints and supplies solver statuses and variables as feedback. OptiMind-SFT weights are not downloaded; presets can connect an independently deployed model service. Current parameters Parameters come from the deployed method preset. They are saved with each run and cannot be changed per run in the UI, CLI or Python API. Parameter Value max_turns 5 temperature 0.6 top_p 0.95 Parameter definitions

title: Choose a library and solver
description: Understand the nine libraries, backend capabilities, AUTO and availability.
text: A modeling library expresses a mathematical model; a backend computes its solution. Start with the variables and constraints, then choose a combination that can express and solve them. Nine modeling libraries Library Typical use Default or native engine Pyomo Algebraic linear, integer and other optimization models Usually HiGHS for algebraic models; CBC for Kernel gurobipy Native Gurobi and matrix modeling Gurobi OR-Tools LP/MIP, CP-SAT, routing, network flows and more Selected for the native interface CPMpy Finite-domain integer, Boolean and global constraints OR-Tools CP-SAT PuLP Linear and mixed-integer programming CBC CVXPY Convex, conic, DGP and DQCP models A native compatible solver path PySCIPOpt Native SCIP linear, integer and nonlinear constraints SCIP CasADi Smooth nonlinear models and other plugin-supported models Ipopt for Opti NLP coptpy Native COPT linear, integer, convex quadratic and conic models COPT Choose a combination For production or transport LP/MILP, begin with Pyomo or PuLP and an open backend. For discrete scheduling and logic, examine CPMpy or OR-Tools CP-SAT. For convex quadratic or conic models, examine CVXPY; for smooth nonlinear models, examine CasADi. Method scope and the installed environment also matter. Selecting CPMpy does not make a continuous decision an integer one. Selecting an LP backend does not relax integer domains. The platform reports incompatibility rather than silently solving a continuous relaxation. AUTO and explicit backends AUTO uses native selection for the library and model. Run settings list backend availability and reasons from the actual sandbox. An explicitly selected backend is not silently replaced after failure. Results record the actual engine. Generated code chooses a library's API, and the platform recognizes the returned native model. OR-Tools MPSolver, MathOpt, CP-SAT and Routing are not four additional library settings. How code reaches the platform Usually, code defines build_model(data) and returns a native model. The platform solves it; generated code does not call solve or print the solution. Routing, network flows and some CasADi APIs also need managers, source/sink nodes or numerical arguments. See the individual pages and native interface notes . A registered backend, a loadable plugin and a usable commercial license are different conditions. See Backends and licenses .

title: Pyomo
description: Express algebraic models and connect compatible native backends.
text: Pyomo expresses algebraic models with sets, parameters, variables, objectives and constraints. It connects to multiple native backends, keeping model expression separate from the engine. Supported interfaces The platform recognizes ConcreteModel , instantiated AbstractModel and pyomo.kernel models. Components such as GDP and DAE remain part of algebraic modeling, rather than extra library settings. Solvability depends on transformations and the selected backend. Select it in the platform Choose Pyomo with AUTO or a native ID from the available backend list. Algebraic models usually default to HiGHS; Kernel automatically uses CBC for its model type. Nonlinear models need a compatible installed backend. uv run llm4om run --problem "Your complete problem" --method direct --language pyomo --solver highs Generated-code requirements build_model(data) returns a constructed native model for the platform to solve. Specify domains and bounds explicitly. Nonnegative integers and continuous variables that may be negative are different decisions. Do not read unsolved variable values while constructing the model. Linear models can use Gurobi IIS evidence under the available diagnosis and license conditions. See Infeasibility . Further reading See official Pyomo modeling documentation , the Kernel API and backend guide . The service discovers actual execution engines from native registries rather than listing decomposition algorithms as engines.

title: gurobipy / Gurobi
description: Use Gurobi's native Python models, matrix API and conflict evidence.
text: gurobipy is Gurobi's native Python modeling interface. Scalar-expression and matrix APIs both return the same native Gurobi model. Select it in the platform Choose gurobipy, whose native engine is Gurobi. Its model is not connected to arbitrary alternative engines. For HiGHS or CBC, use a library with the relevant native adapter. Model capabilities depend on the installed Gurobi version and problem type. The platform retains native constraints and expressions; code must still express domains, objective and requirements correctly. Code and results build_model(data) returns gurobipy.Model without calling optimize() . The platform solves and reads objective, variables, status and available diagnosis. Scalar and matrix APIs may be combined in one model. For an infeasible model, Gurobi IIS can supply conflicting constraints for infeasibility explanation . Evidence concerns the current formulation, so check its mapping to the business requirements. Licenses Without a full license, use is limited to the scope allowed by the runtime. Larger models, shared use and containers require a license suitable for the actual deployment. Configure GRB_LICENSE_FILE and corresponding host, app and sandbox mounts. See Backends and licenses . Official references See the Gurobi Python API and MVar matrix variables . Installation or apparent backend availability does not replace license validation during an actual solve.

title: OR-Tools
description: Use native linear, integer, constraint, routing and network-flow interfaces.
text: OR-Tools provides several native optimization interfaces. The platform has one OR-Tools library setting; code and backend selection determine the native interface. Supported paths Interface Typical tasks MPSolver, MathOpt, ModelBuilder Linear, integer and interface-supported mathematical programming CP-SAT / CpModel Integer, Boolean, logical and discrete scheduling models Routing Vehicle routes and visit sequences Original Constraint Solver Constraint and search models Maximum flow, minimum-cost flow, assignment, knapsack Their respective graph and combinatorial problems Select it in the platform Choose OR-Tools and inspect native backend availability. CP_SAT selects CP-SAT, ROUTING selects Routing, and HIGHS can use MathOpt. The default MPSolver reference uses SCIP. CP-SAT uses integer or Boolean variables rather than continuous decisions. The platform rejects integer models sent to an LP-only backend instead of silently solving a continuous relaxation. Return native models Ordinary mathematical models return the native object. Routing also needs its RoutingIndexManager ; maximum flow needs source/sink; the original Constraint Solver needs variables and optional objective; knapsack needs values, weights and capacities. Native return structures are documented without adding another interface setting. Results and references Short heuristic Routing results are normally feasible ; optimal is retained only when supported by the native status. Interpret graph-algorithm and satisfaction results using their native objective semantics. See the official Python guide , CP-SAT , Routing and MathOpt documentation.

title: CPMpy
description: Model discrete decisions with integer, Boolean and global constraints.
text: CPMpy expresses discrete decisions through integer, Boolean and global constraints. It supports formulations for scheduling, assignment, logic and objective-free satisfaction problems. Modeling scope Variables are finite-domain integers or Booleans, not continuous variables. Fractional data can be scaled to integers when mathematical meaning is preserved; rounding is not a substitute for a continuous decision model. Common global constraints include AllDifferent , Element, Table and Cumulative. Availability depends on native backend support or valid transformations. Select it in the platform Choose CPMpy. Its default is OR-Tools CP-SAT, with native ID ortools . The platform reads base backends and installed subsolvers from SolverLookup. Paths may include CP, SAT, SMT, MIP and MaxSAT, subject to actual deployment availability. Code and results build_model(data) returns cp.Model or a native SolverInterface , without directly calling solve. A model may contain constraints without an objective. A valid assignment is then a satisfaction result and the objective can be empty. An infeasible model can provide MUS conflict constraints for explanation. Actual evidence is required; not every infeasible status automatically yields a business diagnosis. Official references See the CPMpy solver documentation . Check backend installation, domains and diagnosis separately. Registration as a known plugin does not establish that it can run in your environment.

title: PuLP
description: Build linear and mixed-integer models with CBC or other native backends.
text: PuLP builds linear and mixed-integer models with algebraic expressions. It suits LP/MILP problems described through costs, quantities and resource constraints. Supported expression The platform recognizes LpProblem , including row-oriented objectives and constraints and column-oriented modeling through LpConstraintVar . These remain one library choice. Variables can be continuous, integer or binary. Objectives and constraints stay linear; do not directly multiply two decision variables. Use an appropriate formulation or another library for nonlinear relationships rather than omitting them. Select it in the platform Choose PuLP. The default backend is CBC, with native ID PULP_CBC_CMD . The platform uses native listSolvers/getSolver, so available backends are not restricted to CBC. Python, command-line and shared-library interfaces retain their own IDs. Code and checks build_model(data) returns LpProblem without calling solve() . In row-oriented modeling, the first expression added without a comparison becomes the objective. Use unique, stable constraint names for interpretation and checking. Review integer categories, bounds, objective direction and units. Statuses come from the native backend; missing dependencies, incompatibility or license failures retain their actual reasons. Official references See the PuLP modeling API and backend API . Use APIs supported by the deployment's locked version and recheck actual backends after dependency upgrades.

title: CVXPY
description: Model convex optimization and select a backend for its cones and domains.
text: CVXPY constructs optimization problems through expressions and mathematical rules. It supports convex quadratic and conic formulations; the platform also recognizes DGP and DQCP modes. Modeling rules Use DCP-compatible expressions for ordinary convex models. DGP needs its positive-domain and geometric structure, while DQCP needs the corresponding quasiconvex rules. The platform detects the mode from the returned Problem rather than bypassing these rules. Common expressions include sum_squares , norm , quad_form and matrix multiplication @ . Do not use Python if , max or control flow that depends on symbolic variable values. Select a backend AUTO follows CVXPY's native solver_path through installed compatible engines and records the one actually used. Explicit backend selection is not replaced after failure. Example backend What to check OSQP Continuous convex quadratic objectives and linear constraints; no other cones or integer domains Clarabel, SCS Their respective continuous conic capabilities MOSEK and others Problem capabilities, installation and license requirements Integer and Boolean decisions need a compatible mixed-integer backend. Choosing CVXPY does not make a continuous solver valid for them. Code and results build_model(data) returns cvxpy.Problem for platform solving. Results retain native status and numerical-accuracy meanings. The current platform does not provide IIS/MUS explanations for CVXPY. Official references See CVXPY solver features , DGP and DQCP . Actual availability is established by the sandbox backend list and a real solve.

title: PySCIPOpt / SCIP
description: Use native SCIP for linear, integer and nonlinear constraints.
text: PySCIPOpt is SCIP's native Python interface. The platform recognizes its Model with scalar, expression and matrix APIs. Suitable models Native SCIP models express mixed-integer linear problems and supported nonlinear constraints. Direct PySCIPOpt modeling exposes more native structure than the linear SCIP interface within OR-Tools. Capabilities still depend on the installed version and problem type. A method restricted to LP/MILP does not automatically gain a nonlinear modeling workflow by selecting PySCIPOpt. Select it in the platform Choose PySCIPOpt, whose native backend is SCIP. Its Model is not switched to arbitrary alternative engines. Define build_model(data) and return the model without calling optimize() . Express nonlinear objectives The native objective must be linear. Express a nonlinear objective using an auxiliary variable and correctly directed epigraph or hypograph constraints. For example, minimization of a squared expression can bound that expression above by an auxiliary variable and minimize the variable. Check that the transformation preserves the original meaning. Specify bounds explicitly. A continuous decision that may be negative should not accidentally retain a nonnegative default bound. Actual SCIP execution provides the status and objective. Official references See the Model API , nonlinear expressions and matrix interface .

title: CasADi
description: Express smooth nonlinear models and understand plugin and local-solution semantics.
text: CasADi uses symbolic expressions and native plugins for optimization. A common path is Opti with Ipopt for smooth continuous nonlinear models. Supported interfaces The platform supports Opti NLP, Opti Conic and native problem dictionaries for nlpsol , qpsol and conic . Opti returns a model; low-level APIs also need problem structure, numerical arguments, optional plugin and options. Variables follow native ordering. Select it in the platform Choose CasADi, commonly with the Ipopt default. Use smooth expressions and meaningful bounds and initial guesses from the problem. Integer domains require a compatible plugin such as Bonmin; Ipopt is not an integer solver. The platform discovers plugins and checks loading through native CasADi facilities. A loadable plugin does not validate a commercial license. Plugin-specific parameters still follow the native API. Maximization and statuses For maximization through CasADi's minimization interface, minimize the negative objective and return objective_sign: -1 so the platform restores the original value: return { "model" : model, "objective_sign" : - 1 } For nonconvex problems, Ipopt generally provides local conclusions. locally_optimal is not a global certificate, and local infeasibility does not prove the entire problem infeasible. The result page preserves these meanings. Official references See the CasADi documentation and plugin API . If a global conclusion is required, select a suitable global solving approach and check the plugin's actual capabilities in the deployment.

title: coptpy / COPT
description: Use the native COPT interface and check model and license requirements.
text: coptpy is COPT's native Python interface. It is one modeling-library choice, with scalar, expression and matrix APIs returning a COPT model. Modeling scope Current generation guidance covers LP, MILP, convex quadratic and conic optimization. Solvability depends on native capabilities and the installed version. The selected modeling method must also support the problem scope. Select it in the platform Choose coptpy with native engine COPT. Code creates a model through its environment, defines build_model(data) and returns the model without solving. The platform reads the actual objective, variables and native status. This path uses COPT's own model. Choosing COPT as a backend through CVXPY still uses CVXPY as the modeling library, rather than adding another library category. License configuration The current deployment can test examples within the runtime's small noncommercial mode; larger models and commercial deployments need a suitable license. Set COPT_LICENSE_DIR , usually containing license.dat and license.key . Compose also needs matching host-path mounts. The sandbox mounts the actual license files read-only and remains without network access. SDK installation, plugin loading and license validity are separate checks. Missing licenses do not trigger a silent substitute engine. Official references See the COPT Python interface and installation and licensing . Platform mount examples appear in Backends and licenses .

title: Backends and licenses
description: Understand common engines, availability, explicit selection and licenses.
text: The backend list comes from native registries in the actual solver sandbox. First check model and interface compatibility, then dependencies, executables and licenses. Common engine families Engine Typical use and conditions HiGHS, CBC, GLPK Their supported LP/MIP models through compatible libraries SCIP LP/MIP; native nonlinear constraints through PySCIPOpt CP-SAT Integer, Boolean, logical and discrete scheduling models Gurobi, COPT Native mathematical programming, subject to capabilities and licensing Clarabel, SCS Compatible continuous conic models OSQP Continuous convex quadratic programming with linear constraints MOSEK Compatible mathematical programming models; requires a license Ipopt Smooth continuous nonlinear optimization, usually with local conclusions Bonmin Compatible mixed-integer nonlinear plugins through interfaces such as CasADi SAT, SMT, MiniZinc and others Native CPMpy backends, subject to installation This table describes families. Use the platform's current list for exact IDs and availability reasons. One engine may have different library and interface identifiers. AUTO, installation and errors AUTO follows native selection for the library and returned model. Explicit selection is preserved and not replaced after failure. An LP-only backend rejects integer models. Restart the service after changing backend dependencies or licenses to refresh its cache. A registered name does not establish a complete executable installation, and successful plugin loading does not establish commercial-license validity. GPU or separately deployed runtimes need their own environment. Mount licenses Gurobi uses GRB_LICENSE_FILE , MOSEK uses MOSEKLM_LICENSE_FILE , and COPT uses COPT_LICENSE_DIR . Corresponding absolute host and app paths let the sandbox mount required files read-only. For example: services: app: volumes: - /opt/gurobi/gurobi.lic:/opt/gurobi/gurobi.lic:ro - /opt/mosek/mosek.lic:/opt/mosek/mosek.lic:ro Keep only mounts you actually use and set the corresponding .env variables. COPT mounts its individual license.dat and license.key files. The sandbox has no network, so this deployment path needs licenses suitable for offline, container and actual usage conditions. Official license references See Gurobi documentation , MOSEK client setup and COPT installation and licensing . Do not commit license files or keys. The original deployment guide has full container configuration.

title: Team deployment
description: Deploy a shared service with Docker Compose, HTTPS and access controls.
text: A shared deployment centralizes the workbench, model configuration and run records on one server. Members use it through a browser. Complete a single-machine launch before configuring shared access. Use Docker Compose The server needs Docker and Compose v2.24 or later.
