Clone the repository, prepare .env with actual model-service details and start: docker compose up -d --build docker compose ps docker compose logs -f app The app container runs the workbench and LangGraph service. Each solve uses a separate Worker sandbox. The llm4om-data volume stores presets and run history. Configure access and HTTPS The workbench has no built-in login or user-level permissions. People with access can spend shared usage and manage shared records. Restrict team IPs or place an authenticated reverse proxy in front. With a domain, use the included Caddy service: LLM4OM_DOMAIN=llm4om.example.edu LLM4OM_PORT=127.0.0.1:8767 LLM4OM_TRUST_PROXY=1 Point the domain to the server, allow ports 80 and 443, then run: docker compose --profile https up -d --build Replace the example domain with your actual domain. Without one, HTTP can be used on an access-controlled network. Understand execution isolation Generated code runs in network-disabled, read-only, non-root sandboxes that are deleted after completion. The app mounts the host Docker socket, giving it substantial host privileges; deploy on a machine appropriate for that boundary. --sandbox local does not provide this code isolation and is for development. Update and retain data git pull docker compose up -d --build docker compose down stops services while retaining the data volume. Do not remove that volume merely to update. Recreate the app after changing model environment variables. See Configuration for concurrency, usage and backups, and Licenses for commercial engines.

title: Configuration, usage and backups
description: Configure LLMs, concurrency, usage limits and persistent storage.
text: Server configuration controls the default LLM, concurrency, shared usage and persistent storage. Run records retain the settings actually used, without keys. Common environment variables Variable Purpose LLM4OM_LLM_PROVIDER Default preset provider LLM4OM_LLM_BASE_URL Model service endpoint LLM4OM_LLM_MODEL Model ID actually used in API requests LLM4OM_LLM_API_KEY Default preset key LLM4OM_LLM_NAME Preset display name LLM4OM_LLM_EXTRA_BODY Provider-specific request body as JSON LLM4OM_DAILY_TOKENS Daily input-plus-output token limit per preset LLM4OM_RUNS_PER_HOUR Runs per client address per hour LLM4OM_SANDBOX_JOBS Concurrent solves and check scripts across the service; default 4 and must be positive TZ Day boundary for usage accounting, for example Asia/Shanghai LLM4OM_TRUST_PROXY Use the forwarded client address behind a trusted proxy LLM4OM_SEARCH_API_KEY Independent search service key LLM4OM_SEARCH_BASE_URL Independent search endpoint Zero or unset daily-token and hourly-run limits mean unlimited. Exhausted daily usage stops before the next LLM call while retaining completed results. Consult .env.example for exact complete field names. Concurrency and queues llm4om serve --jobs controls active runs, with a default of 4; additional runs queue. LLM4OM_SANDBOX_JOBS separately limits all solves and check scripts, including AutoFormulation's parallel checks. Sandbox waiting counts toward the run deadline. Use one service process per workspace. Keep the same --workspace or Compose volume to retain history. Backup and restore Storage includes preset keys, so restrict backup access. Stop the app, copy the complete workspace and restart: docker compose stop app docker compose cp app:/data ./llm4om-backup chmod -R go-rwx ./llm4om-backup docker compose start app For restoration, stop the service before copying backup contents to /data/ so shutdown writes cannot overwrite restored records. Normal saves occur periodically and at exit; forced termination may lose recent unsaved changes. See the original deployment guide for restoration commands. Optional tracing Enabling LangSmith sends problems, data and model replies to that service. Set LANGSMITH_TRACING and its credentials only when that transfer is permitted. Ordinary platform recording does not require external tracing.

title: CLI and Python
description: Run the same modeling workflows from the CLI or Python.
text: The CLI and Python API execute the same modeling graphs as the server. Use them for scripts, final-state exports and integration with an existing workflow. Run from the CLI With dependencies installed and an LLM configured, run: uv run llm4om run --file problem.txt --method direct --language pyomo --solver highs --output result.json problem.txt is your UTF-8 problem statement. Repeat --data to add attachments: uv run llm4om run --file problem.txt --data demand.csv --data costs.json --method bind --language pyomo The command displays steps and outputs the formulation, code and solver result. --output saves final state and steps. Use --preset for an LLM preset and --workspace for the workspace holding it. Common options Option Meaning --problem / --file Direct problem text or a UTF-8 file --method Method ID, such as direct , feedback_repair or sac_opt --language Library ID, such as pyomo , ortools or cvxpy --solver Native backend ID; omitted means AUTO --data Input attachment; repeatable --sandbox local Host subprocess execution without isolation; development only Per-run calls cannot override method presets. See each method page for actual parameters. Call from Python from llm4om import run_problem state = run_problem( "Produce nonnegative integer quantities A and B, with profits 3 and 2. " "Cutting capacity: 2A+B<=8. Processing capacity: A+2B<=8. " "Maximize total profit." , method= "direct" , language= "pyomo" , solver= "highs" , ) if state.get( "failure" ): print (state[ "failure" ]) else : print (state[ "solve" ][ "objective" ]) Use preset= to select a preset, or llm=LLMSettings(...) to provide model configuration. Selecting a backend does not automatically rewrite a library's API; code and native model must remain compatible.

title: Troubleshooting
description: Resolve connection, LLM, solver and result issues from the actual error.
text: Start with the failed stage and complete error. Distinguish server connection, LLM calls, code execution, infeasibility and method-validation failure before choosing a fix. Platform or LLM connection errors Symptom Next check Cannot connect to the platform Check docker compose ps , listening port, firewall and URL Preset returns 401 Check key, provider and protocol Preset returns 404 Check endpoint and model ID; a display name cannot replace the model ID TriVAL structured output fails with DeepSeek Disable thinking in the run preset as described in LLM presets HTTPS certificate fails Check DNS, ports 80/443 and Caddy logs Code or backend errors For a missing Worker image, rerun docker compose up -d --build , or use uv run llm4om build-worker for a local service. For Docker connection failures, check socket paths and permissions. Expand unavailable-backend reasons and inspect executables, interface type and licensing. Explicit engine selection does not trigger replacement. Do not send continuous decisions to an integer-only model or solve an integer problem with an LP-only backend. An optimal objective with a failure notice Solver optimality concerns the current model. TriVAL or SAC-Opt validation may still fail. Feedback Repair may identify incorrect coefficients, constraints or data binding. Read method feedback and model versions rather than only the objective. If new code fails before execution, it does not inherit the previous solution. Earlier actual solves remain saved in the modeling process. Infeasibility, local results and usage limits For infeasibility, check conflict evidence and business requirements. Local optimality and local infeasibility retain their local meanings; see CasADi . When daily tokens are exhausted, use another available preset or wait for the next day in the configured server timezone. Retrying does not bypass limits. Recover a conversation or report a problem Refresh reconnects to active runs, and failed text replies do not delete saved plans. Preserved steps after cancellation do not imply resuming a method from that node. Record the run link, failed stage, method, library, backend and complete error when reporting a problem. Do not include API keys or license files.
